title: Can Prompt Modifiers Control Bias? A Comparative Analysis of Text-to-Image Generative Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured stereotypical biases in text-to-image models related to religion and culture. Specifically, it evaluated the models' tendency to generate images with strong default associations for religious figures, such as associating the prompt 'Monk' with Asian males and the prompt 'Pastor' with males.
findings: The study found that text-to-image models exhibit strong stereotypical biases for religious/cultural prompts. For the prompt 'Monk', Stable Diffusion and DALL-E 3 strongly defaulted to generating Asian males, even when explicitly prompted for other races (e.g., 'Monk who is Black'). For the prompt 'Pastor', models showed a bias towards generating males. Adobe Firefly consistently produced more balanced and diverse representations for these prompts, indicating a distinct internal approach to bias mitigation. The effectiveness of using prompt modifiers to control these biases varied across models and was not consistently successful.
references: Adobe Systems Incorporated. Adobe firefly: Generative ai for creative processes. https://firefly. adobe.com, 2023. Accessed: 2024-03-24. 2
